I'm so sorry to hear about this and I hope you are doing okay  💔 According to PIBA's protocols, if one of the partners notifies them about a break-up, they should start the file closing procedure according to protocol 5.2.0017 (linked below). According to this protocol, PIBA must summon the couple (together, or you can request separately if you prefer) to a closing interview. The invitation may be sent via physical post. Only after the closing interview, PIBA is allowed to cancel the status of the non-Israeli partner, and the foreign partner is usually given 14 or 30 days to leave Israel. 

Under the procedure, if you have been in Israel for more than half the required 4 years on A5 (it's not clear if you qualify - it could depend on whether you have had visa extensions), and PIBA has no doubts about the honesty of your relationship, your case qualifies to be "automatically" forwarded for a humanitarian status evaluation, as you have completed more than 50% of the required time on A5. This involves an interview where PIBA assess your ties to Israel by looking at all sorts of things. According to the protocol, PIBA is not allowed to revoke your status without an interview or deport you before a final decision has been made, meaning PIBA should theoretically also renew your existing status until a decision has been made.

However, it is important to note that all of this is mostly theoretical. Often PIBA does not do this "automatically". And in practice, obtaining a humanitarian status in Israel is known to be almost impossible, even in cases where there are shared children and shared custody. The humanitarian assessment is known to take years, often they act contrary to the procedure and do revoke status, meaning candidates have no work rights in the meantime. (I note that you can also apply for humanitarian status even if you have not met the 2 year threshold, but that this is "automatic" and this is equally difficult).
